justification: Replaces the email-only builder referral capture with a multi-step qualify-first lead form, stores the qualification answers + an express-consent audit, and adds an /internal/leads admin page (system of record) to read them. Design is evidence-based (CXL qualify-first +20%, OAIC consent rules). Adds first_name/phone/qualification/consent to the canibuildit_leads insert and an additive nullable migration (057). The /internal/leads page is a read-only server component behind the same auth gate as the other /internal pages, reading via the server-only service role. The computed planning verdict is never touched.

pre_impl.existing_data: canibuildit_leads had id/email/address/eligible/created_at/lga_name/interest_type only (verified live). Migration 057 adds first_name, phone, qualification jsonb, consent jsonb — all nullable, so existing rows and the granny-flat/flood/etc. lead paths that reuse this route are unaffected.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Confirmed the route already rate-limits (3/IP/10min), MX-checks the email, and dedups on email+address within 24h; the qualifier rides those unchanged. Confirmed /privacy page exists for the consent link. Smoke-tested that the jsonb columns accept and return the qualification + consent shapes.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Component is a full rewrite of BuilderReferralCard (same file, same single consumer: duplex-check page). Route changes are additive schema fields + additive insert keys. No new endpoint, no change to the verdict computation or to other tools' lead submissions.

functions.name: submit
functions.input: form submit event; reads email, first_name, phone, the four qualification answers, and the shareConsent flag from component state
functions.output: POSTs the lead to /api/canibuildit/lead; sets status to done only on res.ok, else error with an inline message
functions.if_none: If email or consent is missing it sets an inline error and returns without POSTing; if the POST is non-2xx or throws, it shows a retry error and never reaches the success state

functions.name: pick
functions.input: a question key and the selected option value
functions.output: records the answer, emits a referral_qualify_step event, and advances to the next screen
functions.if_none: Budget can be skipped via a Skip control, so a missing budget answer simply advances with budget left null; ownership/timeline/finance are answered by tapping

values: N/A - no DB or external-API values are read to make a decision; the qualification answers are user-supplied option strings validated by a zod enum-length bound, and the consent IP is the server-derived request identifier.

queries.purpose: Duplicate-lead guard — skip insert + email if the same email+address submitted within 24h
Insert the qualified lead + consent audit into the leads system of record
queries.where_clause: N/A - INSERT (append-only lead row); consent/qualification set only when provided, never an UPDATE/DELETE

break_it.scenario: A homeowner completes the qualifier and consents, but the lead insert silently drops the consent audit, leaving no proof of what they agreed to.
break_it.what_happens: Without a stored wording/version/IP/timestamp, a later privacy complaint can't be answered — OAIC puts the burden of proving consent on us.
break_it.how: The route builds a consent record ({version, exact wording, shared_with, server IP, captured_at}) whenever consent_version or consent_wording is present and writes it to the consent jsonb column; smoke-tested that it round-trips.
break_it.repro: Submit the referral form with the consent box ticked, then SELECT consent FROM canibuildit_leads for that row and confirm the exact shown wording, version and IP are present.

break_it.scenario: The migration is not applied in an environment before the new code deploys there, so the insert references columns that don't exist.
break_it.what_happens: Supabase would reject the insert; because the insert is in a non-blocking try/catch the lead would be lost silently.
break_it.how: Migration 057 is additive and idempotent (ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS) and has been applied to the single production Supabase DB; the new insert keys are spread conditionally so a row still inserts even if a given qualification/consent value is absent.
break_it.repro: On a DB without 057, POST a qualified lead and confirm the columns are missing; after applying 057, confirm the same POST stores qualification + consent.

break_it.scenario: The trimmed 3-step qualifier collects only timeline + ownership; finance and budget are always sent null. The /internal/leads view or later reporting could assume all four qualifiers are present and break or mislabel.
break_it.what_happens: A qualification object with finance/budget null could render empty/undefined chips or throw on a missing field.
break_it.how: The qualification jsonb carries explicit nulls for finance/budget; the /internal/leads display maps each field through label() (returns null when absent) and .filter(Boolean), so only present qualifiers render; the zod schema marks every qualification field optional/nullable.
break_it.repro: Submit a lead via the 3-step form; confirm qualification jsonb = {timeline, ownership, finance:null, budget:null} and /internal/leads shows only the timeline + ownership chips.

break_it.scenario: Someone who is not signed in guesses the /internal/leads URL to read lead PII (name, email, phone, address, IP, consent).
break_it.what_happens: If the page rendered open it would leak the whole leads table — a privacy breach worse than the other /internal pages because this is raw consented PII.
break_it.how: Unlike the other /internal pages (gated only when NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_ENABLED==='true'), /internal/leads is fail-closed: it ALWAYS calls supabase.auth.getUser() and redirects unauthenticated visitors to /login, independent of any env flag. It is also noindex. Trade-off: viewing leads now requires being logged in.
break_it.repro: With NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_ENABLED unset and no session, visit /internal/leads and confirm it redirects to /login (does NOT render the table); confirm it renders once signed in.

break_it.scenario: A bot posts to the lead endpoint with the honeypot filled or an invalid email domain.
break_it.what_happens: Junk leads would pollute the qualified-lead pipeline the builders pay for.
break_it.how: Unchanged existing guards: the honeypot 'website' field returns a silent ok without inserting, the MX check rejects non-deliverable domains with a 400, and the per-IP rate limit caps submissions — the qualifier sits on top of these.
break_it.repro: POST with website set to non-empty and confirm no row inserts; POST with an @nonexistentdomain.invalid email and confirm a 400.

post_merge.db_reset: Not required. Migration 057 (additive nullable columns on canibuildit_leads) is already applied to production Supabase; no data change, no backfill.
post_merge.secrets: No new secrets. Uses the existing server-only Supabase service-role credential already configured for this route.
post_merge.other_repo: None. Frontend + its API route only; the leads live in the same Supabase. The /internal/leads admin view is now built (read-only); status/routing/HubSpot-sync remain scoped in ce-lead-qualifier-research-2026-07.md.
post_merge.auth: /internal/leads is now fail-closed — it always requires a signed-in user (redirects to /login) regardless of NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_ENABLED, so the PII page can't render open. The other /internal pages (index, setback-review, dcp-review) still use the flag-based gate; rolling the same fail-closed pattern to them is a follow-up. To view leads you must be logged in.
post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - on the preview: run an eligible address, tap through timeline/ownership/finance, skip budget, enter contact + tick consent, submit; confirm the success state and then that a canibuildit_leads row has the qualification and consent jsonb populated (incl. the exact consent wording and an IP). Also confirm the needs-checking result shows the same qualifier with 'specialist' wording.
